title: How is the unused-credit value of a class-credit pack calculated before it is refunded?
content:
## Scope
This document covers the Group Fitness Class Passes product line. It states how the value of a pack's unused credits, and the refund amount before any further adjustment, are determined when a refund is being valued.

## Reconciling the true remaining balance
The pack's true remaining credit balance is reconciled from its complete credit-ledger history: the credits originally included by its tier (zero for the Unlimited Monthly Classes tier, which grants unlimited use rather than a finite credit count) plus the net sum of every credit change recorded against this pack across its entire history to date. This reconciled figure, not the tier's original credit count taken alone, feeds the valuation below.

## Valuing the unused credit
The tier's own proration basis decides which of two valuations applies. Under a credits-used basis, the unused-credit value is the reconciled remaining balance divided by the tier's included credit count, multiplied by the tier's purchase price. Under a percentage-elapsed basis, the unused-credit value is the tier's purchase price multiplied by one minus the fraction of the tier's expiration window already elapsed, counted in whole calendar days from the pack's purchase date and measured against the current date.

## Refund amount before further adjustment
The refund amount before any further adjustment is the unused-credit value multiplied by the tier's refund percentage.

## Hypothetical worked example (illustration only)
Suppose, purely for illustration, a credits-used tier includes 20 credits at a purchase price of $240.00, its refund percentage is 85 percent, and the pack's reconciled remaining balance is 8 credits. The unused-credit value is 8 divided by 20, multiplied by $240.00, giving $96.00; the refund amount before further adjustment is 85 percent of $96.00, giving $81.60.

## Points of judgement
- The reconciled balance reflects every booking, cancellation and prior partial refund already recorded; the valuation never uses the tier's original credit count in isolation once any such history exists.
- Which valuation basis applies is fixed by the tier itself, never selected case by case.
